transcript: Last night, I saw Daphne, a new play at Lincoln Center. Daphne lives with her girlfriend Winona in “the middle of nowhere” and the entire play takes place in their secluded home. There's an overall sense of uneasiness — about the house, the pet bird hidden under a sheet the entire time, and the tense dynamic between Daphne and Winona. Daphne seems especially uneasy in this house and it's compounded by the fact that her skin is slowly transforming into what appears to be tree bark throughout the play. I have to admit, I found this whole thing somewhat bizarre and incomprehensible, but my interpretation is that Daphne is, in a sense, drowning and losing herself in the harsh and isolating relationship that Winona controls. It’s an interesting premise, but I wish the play could have better connected its surreal direction with its emotional through line. With that, another program for my collection.
